safety_observation.name: safety_observation
safety_observation.description: A safety observation refers to any recorded note or report about workplace conditions, behaviors, or practices that may impact health and safety. These observations are typically made by workers, supervisors, or safety personnel during routine checks or daily activities to identify both safe and unsafe practices. They help in proactively identifying trends and preventing incidents.
examples: Observed worker wearing proper PPE in the welding area.
Noted that emergency exits were clear during shift change.
Identified safe lifting practices being followed in warehouse.
Observed forklift operator using seatbelt as required.
Noted that spill kits were fully stocked and accessible.

near_miss.name: near_miss
near_miss.description: A near miss is an unplanned event that did not result in injury, illness, or damage but had the potential to do so. In HSE, near misses are reported to identify hazards and prevent future incidents by addressing underlying causes before harm occurs.
examples: A falling tool narrowly missed a worker's foot but caused no injury.
Forklift reversed into a walkway but stopped before hitting anyone.
Chemical container slipped but was caught before spilling.
Worker tripped over hose but regained balance and was not hurt.
Overhead load swung unexpectedly but did not strike any personnel.

incident.name: incident
incident.description: An incident is any unplanned event that results in or could have resulted in injury, illness, property damage, or environmental harm. In HSE, incidents are formally reported and investigated to determine root causes and prevent recurrence.
examples: Worker sustained a laceration while using a box cutter.
Oil spill occurred during equipment maintenance.
Employee slipped on wet floor and sprained ankle.
Fire alarm triggered due to electrical short circuit.
Forklift collided with storage rack causing minor damage.

hazard_report.name: hazard_report
hazard_report.description: A hazard report documents the identification of a potential source of harm or danger in the workplace. These reports are used to alert management and safety teams to risks that need to be assessed and controlled to prevent incidents.
examples: Reported exposed wiring near the loading dock.
Identified unguarded machinery in production area.
Noted chemical storage area lacking proper signage.
Reported loose handrail on main staircase.
Observed blocked fire extinguisher access.

environmental_observation.name: environmental_observation
environmental_observation.description: An environmental observation records any condition or event that may impact the environment, such as pollution, waste, or wildlife disturbances. In HSE, these observations help monitor compliance with environmental regulations and identify areas for improvement.
examples: Observed oil sheen on surface water near outfall.
Noted excessive dust emissions from conveyor belt.
Reported improper disposal of chemical containers.
Identified wildlife nesting near storage tanks.
Observed waste bins overflowing in outdoor area.

quality_issue.name: quality_issue
quality_issue.description: A quality issue refers to any observation or report of a product, process, or service not meeting established standards or specifications. In HSE, quality issues can relate to defective equipment, substandard materials, or process deviations that may also pose safety or environmental risks.
examples: Found welds not meeting inspection criteria on pressure vessel.
Reported batch of safety gloves with torn seams.
Identified mislabeled chemical drums in storage.
Noted paint finish defects on equipment panels.
Observed incorrect assembly of machine guards.

maintenance_request.name: maintenance_request
maintenance_request.description: A maintenance request is a formal notification to repair, replace, or service equipment, infrastructure, or safety systems. In HSE, timely maintenance requests help prevent equipment failures, unsafe conditions, and ensure compliance with safety standards.
examples: Requested repair of leaking hydraulic hose on forklift.
Submitted work order for malfunctioning emergency lighting.
Reported broken guardrail on mezzanine platform.
Requested servicing of air quality monitoring system.
Notified maintenance of faulty fire alarm panel.

unsafe_condition.name: unsafe_condition
unsafe_condition.description: An unsafe condition is any physical state or environmental factor in the workplace that could lead to injury, illness, or property damage. Reporting unsafe conditions is critical in HSE to eliminate hazards before they result in incidents.
examples: Wet floor in corridor without warning signs.
Unsecured ladder left in walkway.
Damaged electrical outlet near water source.
Poor lighting in stairwell area.
Obstructed emergency exit door.

unsafe_act.name: unsafe_act
unsafe_act.description: An unsafe act is any behavior or action by a person that increases the risk of an accident or injury. In HSE, these acts are observed and reported to correct unsafe behaviors and reinforce safe work practices.
examples: Worker bypassed machine guard during operation.
Employee climbed shelving to reach high item.
Operator used mobile phone while driving forklift.
Technician failed to lock out equipment before maintenance.
Worker did not wear required eye protection in lab.
